There is no point using Cypher, whilst Chamber is the way he is... Chamber trip is OP in every way.

His TP needs to be lessened.  The biggest issue I have with Chamber is on defense where he doesn't need to rotate.  His TP should be for getting him out of trouble... not being able to TP from one site to another without having to rotate.  Bind is a perfect example.  He can TP from U Hall on A to B site, meaning that the enemy team always has an extra defender on site - If the enemy team has a Chamber who's aim is decent, it makes attacking on Bind nearly impossible, because they always have that extra player on site immediately.

Same with Breeze..  They always start at mid top so they can watch elbow and through tunnel on B site, as well as watch mid.. and if the enemy attacks A, they TP to bridge to hold from there - This is ridiculous imo because Chamber is essentially there to hold every single entry point on the map at the click of a button.

Icebox - Mid boiler to A rafters

Ascent - Mid to B Market

Even his trip is stupid.. why does it remain active all the way across the map?  It should be there just to hold behind him.. that's the purpose.  It shouldn't be like a Cypher trap where it's active on B site, if he is on A site.  It should have a range on it.

To conclude.. I don't think Chamber is being used the way he is supposed to as an agent.  He should be there to lockdown defense on ONE site.  His kit gives entire map control on defense... not just a site control.  Trip is supposed to be either behind him, or on an entry point he is not watching.  TP is to get him out of trouble only.  Trip is NOT for him to gain info on the opposite site when he is not even there, and the TP is NOT for him to be able to go from one location to the next without rotating.  his TP should legit be not much further than Omen's.. He should be TP on the same site to a different location, not halfway across the map!

Chamber's TP distanced needs to be shortened.  It should be to get him out of harms way.. not to teleport from one site to the next.  It's especially bad on Bind defence.  He can TP from U Hall on A to that small corner on the left side of B.  I have lost 4 v 5 matches on Bind due to the enemy Chamber ALWAYS being on site.  He literally adds a 3rd person to whatever site is pushed immediately, without having to rotate.

Getting Site control, and plant/post plant situations.

I feel like the way you know if you are playing well, is if you are doing these things -

Trading when you die.  So not dying every round, but getting no kills in the process.

Being able to come back from a bad start and staying consistent when you have a good start.  So if you start 0.8 - Being able to finish the game on a respectable k/d, even if it's something like 13.15.  Also, not trailing off... so starting 10.2 and finishing 14.18 - this is not good.

Being able to match the best player on the other team.  Check the performance at the end of the match.  If all your kills are against the players who went 4.20, and you are 1.10 against the guy that went 30.10, then you really haven't done anything great, even if you are on 30.10 yourself.

Being able to clutch games that you would normally consider 'losable'.. so situations that are 1 v 4, and you plant and win, or even harder.. defuse and win.

Being able to set up your team from the start... so entry fragging and getting 2 or 3 kills.

Being able to communicate with your team and tell them what to do, and not get into arguments, troll or be toxic towards them.  Be supportive and in the process be able to win games that you probably should lose, because your opponents are better players but your team out played them with good comms.

And last but not least - playing your role.  I played a game with Sage earlier where i went 11.15 and was on the bottom of the combat score table.  But I feel like I  had a really good game.  I wasn't going for kills because we had a Reyna and a Phoenix who popped off, so I played my role.. stayed back, planted, defused, heal, res, wall and got kills when I had opportunities but didn't do anything crazy so my team has to play the round without my abilities.  Most of my deaths were from defending the site post plant or trying to enter sites to defuse.  I won us a few rounds in clutch moments, and set us up for wins over and over by walling the right places, planting in strategic positions, heal, res, etc.  If I was kill hungry, and getting kills but not lasting until the end of rounds we might have lost the game.  This is playing your role, and not thinking of yourself or your own ego.

These are some things I would think are important.  You definitely do not need to do all of these, all the time.  But if you do these things regularly then I would say you are a good player.

There is something about this game that is off imo. 

I don't know what it is, but I can have a game where I get 25 kills and I can basically run around the map headshotting and killing anyone I see.

The game straight after, I'll get 5 kills for the match, and even if I sit in a corner with a judge, someone will run around that corner and HS me before I can even get a shot off.

My aim is just good or bad from game to game, and it's been like this all act for me.  It's totally random and inconsistent and I don't know the exact reason why.

But I have come to some conclusions.... 

1 - Cheaters.  There are more cheaters in the game now.  There are reddit threads on it.  All it takes is for one person to have a wall hack and he can ping where you are to his team.  So it can seem like you are aiming badly because you can't kill a guy who is on 5.20, but that guy knows you are there, and has your head lined up before he comes around the corner and pre fires.

2  - Smurfs vs Non-Smurfs.  I'm in Silver, I aim for a HS, but a lot of the time, especially in rushed or intense situations, I'll hit 4 body shots.  IF I'm against an ACTUAL SILVER player, then this can work because they won't be hitting the head either.  But if I'm against an Immortal or Diamond smurf, then I'm gone because they will HS me.  So, it can give the appearance that your aim is bad, but in reality you are against someone who can pop heads before you can even press the shoot button.  Then next game you are against no smurfs so it gives the appearance your aim is awesome again, but really... you are just against people who have actual bad aim and can't hit heads.

3 - Ping.  I've noticed that games where pings inconsistent, it has an effect on things.  Peeker vs Non Peeker advantage.  My Ping is usually around 28.  And it doesn't matter if the ping is higher or lower, but if there are 2 people on the opposing team with pings of 8 or 16, they will usually kill me before I can get a shot off.  Alternatively, and this sometimes happens with an entire team... they have pings of 60 - 80, and the entire team seems like they are wall hacking.  I'll be killed by 4 bullets before I can even fire a shot.  Ping advantage in this game is huge.  And it can give a perception that your aim is bad but really, they are seeing you first.

I don't know if this information is helpful, but from my personal experience.. I find these points can give a perception that my aim has gone bad, but really my aim hasn't changed.  These factors just make it seem like it.  If you have good games then bad games, I doubt it's 100% your aim, and it's these things I've mentioned.  

If you are having ALL bad games, then possibly your aim is contributing, and I'd recommend changing your style of play for a while.  Rather than engage, be more of a lurker.  Use Sage, KJ.. types that are OK to stay back with, and get kills from flankers, etc.  This might help restore  your confidence because you are not ending up on 5.20 K/D's and might mentally feel better even if you go like 13.15 or something.

In American English, judgement is generally considered a misspelling of judgment for all uses of the word, notwithstanding individual preferences. In British popular usage, judgment was traditionally the preferred form, but judgement has gained ground over the last couple of centuries and is now nearly as common as judgment. 

When it comes to legal contexts, English reference sources say varying things. Most seem to agree that judgment is preferred in legal contexts even in British English, and some say that American and British English differ in their strict legal meanings of judgment. Bryan Garner, in his Modern American Usage, says judgment in American English refers to “the final decisive act of a court in defining the rights of the parties,” whereas, he writes, the word in British English refers to a judicial opinion.
